title: The Lord's Mercy and the Transformation of Mourning
english: I have cried out to the High Priest as a physician, and I will help toward my God, without dividing the Father from the Son. He who cries out to God cries out toward the Trinity; for the Trinity is one God, not the same as the numerical identity, if it is necessary to speak of numbers.

What profit is there in my blood, in my descending into corruption? I descended into corruption; what profit has occurred? Behold, they remain in their own evils. But he does not say this at all. Rather it is said: 'you were bought' with the blood of Christ, and that: 'not with corruptible things, silver and gold, were you redeemed from your vain manner of life, but in precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish and spotless, Christ' (1 Pet 1:18-19). And this is possible: the whole sum of the saved is called the Body of Christ.

Since, therefore, the Savior arrived and received all that we previously mentioned—the darkness and the cross and the descent into Hades—not all returned, not all took up virtue and faith, but some and others; according to this he says: 'he turned my face away' (Ps 49:15) from certain things being members of me, being my body, 'and I became troubled.' If, therefore, he saved and redeemed and set free by his own blood, how does he say: 'what profit is there in my blood, in my descending into corruption?' Much profit has occurred—but toward those who remain in evils. As for how much has reached you, no profit has exceeded in my blood, my descending into corruption. He says, moreover, that he stirs them up toward repentance.

For this reason he has said: 'shall dust confess to you or announce your truth?' (Ps 65:2) Behold, there are some being dust. But I have come to suffer, so that I might transform them and make them heavenly from being swine. Since, therefore, they remain still wearing the image of the swine, they do not confess to you, nor do they even announce your truth. But I have come so that I might also make the truth manifest, exposing the wandering and the falsehood, and so that I might grant confession, so that someone might cast off the image of the swine and take up that of the heavenly. He says therefore: 'shall dust confess to you?' If dust does not confess to you, as much as has reached him, no profit from my blood has exceeded my descending into corruption. Then—since I have said...

He says this because of those being pressed by former evils; and we have confessed that he also redeemed many by his own blood—thus demonstrating them. 11 The Lord heard and had mercy on me (Ps 117:2). By showing the mercy of the Lord, he speaks of their salvation, that they might receive mercy. 11 The Lord became a helper to me. The verb 'became' signifies that they were not previously so: 'A helper and a protector became to me for salvation.' 11 The Lord heard and had mercy on me (Ps 117:2). I was lamenting, because having descended into corruption, no benefit from my blood has occurred to anyone; but building up the pitied ones, and demonstrating those who are at their peak to be such, that they shall one day be saved; the medicine will one day work in them.

12 You turned my mourning into joy for me (Ps 30:11). He was cutting away the dead out of philanthropy, so that he might raise them up; for immediately a certain understanding took hold: if he mourns and laments because of my sinning, I owe much more to do this. Therefore, 'You turned my mourning into joy for me': their benefit is joy to me, and when we were sinning, my lamentation and mourning were theirs. 12 Having torn my sackcloth, you girded me with gladness. I was carrying a sackcloth of mourning, a severe life, rough, but he changed it into gladness. Thus we have also spoken regarding: 'If in Tyre and Sidon the powers became, long ago they would have repented sitting in sackcloth and ashes' (Matt 15:28; Jonah 2:5). We say that the name of the sackcloth signifies the severe, bitter, and cleansing life of the one lamenting. After this sackcloth, someone takes ashes and sits, no longer acting against it, but sits, ceasing the anger of evil. He groaned over this, which bore chaff, thorns, and thistles; for he was not able to sit among the thorns and thistles, but having burned them and shown them powerless, and that quality by which they were vile, having risen up, he sat upon them.

13 So that my glory may sing to you and I may not be dejected (Ps 82:1). Some say a hint: 'I shall not be dejected'; while my glory sings to you, I am not dejected. But this reading does not satisfy me. Many in the church read it this way. The term 'dejection' (katanyxis) often signifies a repentance. For when Ahaz repented:
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Hope and Divine Justice
english: "Did you see how Ahaz was consoled?" and "you gave them a spirit of consolation," a spirit of repentance. This is therefore what he says: my glory sings to you, I act according to your will, and I do not repent, I am not brought low by sorrow. He is not brought low as if by evil, so as to no longer be active. Therefore he connects [the thought] and says: "Lord, my God, I will give thanks to you forever" (Ps 116:17). "Lord, my God, I will give thanks to you forever." Since, therefore, I will give thanks to you forever, singing to your glory, I am not brought low, nor do I repent.

To the end: A psalm of David; of ecstasy. The name of ecstasy is homonymous; for it signifies many things, one of which is deviation or folly; the one who wanders is in ecstasy (stands outside himself). But the name of ecstasy also signifies wonder; for he who wonders is said to be in ecstasy (standing outside himself): "I perceived your works and was amazed" (Ps 138:14) having seen their greatness, the art by which they came to be. And there are many expressions declaring that wonder is made manifest by the name of ecstasy. Thus also Isaac "was in great ecstasy" when he received the blessing from Isaac. And again, ecstasy signifies becoming something outside of one's former state, as if he says: "But I said in my ecstasy, 'Every man is a liar'" (Ps 123:4). When he stood outside himself and was no longer a man, but had become God by making room for the Word of God coming to him, then he said: "Every man is a liar"; for if we take this simply, he lies. If every man is a liar and he himself is one of men, he lies. But in him saying "every man is a liar," they are not altogether liars. The things of men are uncertain, unstable. Such is also what the apostle says: "What eye has not seen, and what ear has not heard, and what has not ascended into the heart of man" (1 Cor 2:9). He is not, therefore, [merely] the same man, but he brings forth: "But God has revealed them to us through the Spirit" (1 Cor 2:10), to us who are no longer [merely] men, those who are able to say with boldness: "We have stood in ecstasy with God, we are of the same mind with you." He, therefore, who says these things in the psalm was also in ecstasy; he has become another, he has become God by participating in the Word of God; he has ceased to be a man. For certainly, observe that he does not speak human things, but things that it is fitting for a man having been made divine to proclaim.

And to sing. Upon you, Lord, I have hoped, that I might not be put to shame for ever (Psalm 25:3). For I am not put to shame when the things of the petition exist; for then the one praying suffers shame when he does not happen to get what he expected. And if we take 'the age' more simply, this says: in the time of my life, let me not be put to shame, always attaining those things which I entreat to receive from you; for it has been said many times that the time extending the life of man is called 'an age', just as: 'I will not eat meat for ever'. And it is possible also to say thus: since you are eternal and your existence and your kingdom extend through all the ages, and I too am immortal according to the soul, 'let me not be put to shame for ever'; for I am always with you. Now I know in part and I prophesy, but the one who is perfect will receive that which is in part, so that my hope becomes greater, having a greater remainder of expectation. Therefore, the one who hopes in the Lord is without shame.

Save me in your righteousness and bring me out (Psalm 70:1). The beginning of this seventieth [psalm] has a certain kinship and likeness. And in the seventieth lies the 'bring me out' itself, concerning which it is said: 'righteousness bowed down', when having bent the heaven, it came down. It has come to loose injustice; for the world having come about on earth was full of injustice; for 'the earth was filled' with iniquities (Genesis 6:13), just as before the flood, when 'all turned aside, at the same time they sinned, there is no one doing goodness' (Genesis 6:11). Just as the light rises and becomes there where the darkness is, and the darkness is made manifest by the presence of light, and when virtue shines forth, evil is driven away—so, when righteousness is revealed and those entreating it are saved, all injustice is dissolved.

Incline your ear toward me, hasten to bring me out (Psalm 70:5). Even if I cry out to you, I am small-voiced as toward your majesty. If you do not incline your ear toward me, my cry is not able to ascend to you. If you do not descend with me, you will not receive my voice. And in another way: since he does not observe all the lawlessness of those being judged and examined by him, it is necessary for him to incline the ear, so that he may hear; for whatever kind of knowledge and whatever kind of power...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Spirit and the Soul in God's Hands
english: The prayer remains, and does not ascend to him if it does not incline toward him; but it inclines by descending together. When you incline your ear to me, receive me and quickly take me out from those holding me, from those attacking me. Even if enemies are, 'quickly let me be delivered' (Ps 145:14). Did he say these things in amazement? He did not say that foolishness is shown here, but rather the wonder of becoming outside of himself. You are ignorant of this, that there is not one single perfection. For the one having been perfected says: 'I have seen the end of every arrangement' (Ps 71:20); for he does not say these things having an end that is beyond all.

Become for me, O God, a protector and a house of refuge to save me (Ps 18:2). Become for me an invincible fortress, an unpierceable wall; become for me also a protector, your shield, your weapon. When you become my protector, none of my enemies can harm me. A beast cannot overcome me, the very one snatching, about whom we were sending a prayer: 'never snatch my soul like a lion' (Ps 18:48). 'And into a house of refuge' (Ps 18:49). Become for me that which is called a stronghold, where one fleeing enters within walls; for a building is a guard by means of salvation.

For you are my strength and my refuge (Ps 18:2). You are everything to me, both strength and refuge. I flee to no one, not to a ruler, nor to wealth. And my strength: from you I have the power to hold fast, participating in you, just as a king holds fast. For the sake of your name, you will guide me and nourish me (Ps 143:8). He says this because since your name is called upon me, because of this name of yours which I wear, grant both to me; and guide me, so that I may finish the race without fault and be able to say: 'I have run without lawlessness and I have directed my course' (2 Tim 4:7), and: 'I have run the path of your commandments' (Ps 119:30). And let me be nourished by you. Your way and bread is your Son. 'Way' is he saying, 'I am the way' (John 14:6). He himself is both way and bread. Therefore, 'for the sake of your name,' which you granted to me, so that I may have salvation; for I grew and said: 'O God, in your name save me.'

Bring me out of this snare which you hid for me (Ps 124:7), because you are my protector. Enemies are many, some deceivers, they have prepared a snare for me, so that they may hunt me. I do not only entreat that you may not let me depart there, but also...

Unless they enter, so that you might lead me out from it. One must examine and thus [see] 5–6: 'for you are my protector, into your hands I will commit my spirit' (Psalm 31:5). I do not commit my spirit to another, but into your hands.

And if a holy man is the one saying these things, his spirit is that which is joined to the soul, concerning which it is said: 'your whole spirit and soul and body.' Some say the spirit is something other than the soul, others [say it is] its mind, and others [say] its will. But in all these interpretations, God preserves the spirit. If it is the soul, it is committed into the hands of God so that, being covered, it might remain unharmed, not being struck by enemies, not being destroyed.

Because it is sometimes said that the soul is spirit, Stephen teaches; for as he was about to die, and he exhorted [them] not to let the sin of those murdering him stand, he says: 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit' (Acts 7:59), instead of 'my soul.' And James writes: 'just as the body without spirit is dead' (James 2:26), calling the soul spirit. And it is said, as I have said, that something rational is also joined to it, like an inseparable thing, so that it might be a teacher of the soul, [namely] spirit.

And since this belongs to the soul when it possesses God, he says this: 'may such a thing not happen to me, so that my spirit might be outside your hands, but may all virtue be made straight for me, so that my spirit might be in your hands.' It is also possible to call one's will 'spirit,' so that he also wants it to be guarded in the hands of God.

Therefore, also the interpretative [points]: the two covenants can be the hands of God. Into these, then, I commit my spirit, wanting to understand both the old, that is, those things protected there, and the new. May both your hands contain my spirit. And it is possible also to say not only two hands of God; for it was not spoken in the dual, but in the plural; and there is no difference between the plural and the dual. However, if the two covenants exist, the hands are spoken of in the dual. But if all the power of God is named his hand—for we say 'the hand of a king' regarding military power—into your military power, finding it to be a guarding hand, I commit my spirit. Toward the...
